question: Should a high-volume, low-price gym operator open in tier-2 Indian cities, or hold in metros?
lessons_narrative: Cheap rent does not rescue a weak contribution margin. Test the unit before you test the map.
outcome: Positive club-level contribution margin within 18 months of opening.
background: The operator runs 40 clubs in six metros on a low-price, high-volume membership model. Metro rents have risen 30% in three years while price competition has capped membership fees.
complication: Growth capital has been raised against a 100-club target. Metro economics no longer clear the hurdle rate, so the board is pushing tier-2 expansion on the assumption that cheaper rent fixes the model.
recommendation: Hold on tier-2. Rent is not the binding constraint; member density and retention are. Fix retention in three metro clubs first, then expand on a proven unit.

reasons.claim: Rent is a smaller share of cost than assumed
reasons.hypothesis: If rent were the binding constraint, then rent would exceed 30% of club-level cost.
reasons.test_method: Rebuilt club P&L from disclosed cost lines across the metro estate.
reasons.data_source: Company filings; comparable listed operators' club-level disclosures.

reasons.claim: Retention, not acquisition, is the leak
reasons.hypothesis: If retention were healthy, then member lifetime would exceed the payback period on acquisition cost.
reasons.test_method: Compared average member tenure against blended CAC payback.
reasons.data_source: Internal cohort data; industry retention benchmarks.

reasons.claim: Tier-2 density does not support the volume model
reasons.hypothesis: If tier-2 catchments could support the model, then addressable members within 3km would match metro catchments.
reasons.test_method: Catchment sizing across five candidate cities against the metro benchmark.
reasons.data_source: Census density data; income distribution by city tier.

risks: The retention diagnosis rests on cohort data from a single region; if churn is regionally idiosyncratic, the conclusion weakens.
next_steps: Run a 90-day retention intervention in three metro clubs. Re-underwrite the tier-2 case only once member lifetime clears CAC payback.
disclaimer: Based on publicly available information. Illustrative analysis, not investment advice.
